root_cause.text: The dpaa2-switch driver trusted the firmware-provided `sw_attr.num_ifs` without bounding it against `DPSW_MAX_IF`, so `dpaa2_switch_fdb_get_flood_cfg()` could index past its fixed-size `cfg->if_id[64]` array when populating flood-port and control-interface IDs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs >= DPSW_MAX_IF) { ... -EINVAL; }` in `dpaa2_switch_init()`, and the CVE description says `num_ifs` “controls iteration in dpaa2_switch_fdb_get_flood_cfg(), which writes port indices into the fixed-size cfg->if_id[DPSW_MAX_IF] array” and that when `num_ifs >= 64` the loop can write past the array bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to reject switches reporting too many interfaces during initialization.
intent_record.what: A new validation block was added in dpaa2_switch_init() after reading sw_attr: if ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs is greater than or equal to DPSW_MAX_IF, the code logs an error message, sets err to -EINVAL, and jumps to err_close.
intent_record.how: This prevents the driver from continuing initialization when the switch reports more interfaces than the driver’s maximum supported interface count, avoiding out-of-bounds or unsupported interface handling later in setup.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check to reject switches reporting too many interfaces during initialization.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by bounding the firmware-provided interface count during initialization, preventing later out-of-bounds indexing of the fixed-size if_id array.

candidates.rationale: This initialization path continues using firmware-provided switch attributes without any prior upper bound check on the number of interfaces, allowing later code to trust an unchecked sw_attr.num_ifs and potentially overflow fixed-size interface arrays.

vuln_statements.explanation: This initialization path is part of the code that accepts firmware-reported switch attributes before any upper-bound validation on sw_attr.num_ifs. By failing to reject an excessive number of interfaces here, later code could trust the unchecked value and overflow the fixed-size cfg->if_id[64] array in dpaa2_switch_fdb_get_flood_cfg().

In this commit the switch object is created from MC-provided data and later code in this driver uses those attributes to fill per-interface arrays. The vulnerability root cause says `sw_attr.num_ifs` was not bounded against `DPSW_MAX_IF`, allowing `dpaa2_switch_fdb_get_flood_cfg()` to index past `cfg->if_id[64]`.
